reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports the general concept that an inverted BCC+B2 microstructure improves ductility while maintaining high yield strength at room and elevated temperature, but it does not provide specific support for the claimed 20–30% yield strength improvement, the precise precipitate size/volume fraction targets, or the long-term coarsening resistance at 700–1000 °C.
premises: B2 precipitates in a BCC matrix can improve ductility while maintaining high yield strength at room and elevated temperature.
The 'inverted' microstructure with discrete B2 precipitates in a continuous BCC matrix is achievable via microstructural engineering.
The proposed bimodal microstructure will improve elevated-temperature mechanical properties specifically for refractory HEAs.
Fine B2 precipitates (10–50 nm, 10–20% volume fraction) will resist coarsening and act as effective dislocation barriers during prolonged high-temperature service.
The intervention will yield a 20–30% improvement in elevated-temperature yield strength compared to a single-phase BCC HEA.
